title: Warm-up: C's division from floor division
starter:
%a = param [] slot=0 dtype=i32 addrspace=ALU
%b = param [] slot=1 dtype=i32 addrspace=ALU
%out = div %a %b
hints: Floor and truncation only disagree when the exact quotient is negative and not whole. Then floor is one lower.
Compute `q = div a b` and `r = mod a b`. Truncation needs `q + 1` exactly when `r` is nonzero and a and b have opposite signs.
Build both conditions as bools: nonzero is `r < 0` xor `0 < r`, and opposite signs is `a < 0` xor `b < 0`. `where c1 c2 false` is an AND.
prompt: .uir's div floors. C's / truncates toward zero, and you'll render C in week 2, so it pays to know exactly where they differ. Build C's truncating division as %out, from div, mod, cmplt, xor, where and add. The tests never divide by zero.

answer.code:
%a = param [] slot=0 dtype=i32 addrspace=ALU
%b = param [] slot=1 dtype=i32 addrspace=ALU
%q = div %a %b
%r = mod %a %b
%rneg = cmplt %r 0
%rpos = cmplt 0 %r
%nz = xor %rneg %rpos
%aneg = cmplt %a 0
%bneg = cmplt %b 0
%opp = xor %aneg %bneg
%fix = where %nz %opp false
%q1 = add %q 1
%out = where %fix %q1 %q
answer.explain: Floor division rounds down, so when the true quotient is negative and has a fractional part, it lands one below C's truncated answer. The reference detects that case (a nonzero remainder and operands of opposite signs) with `cmplt` and `xor`, ANDs the two with a `where`, and adds one only then. `INT_MIN div -1` wraps to `INT_MIN` in both.
